questions.q: What is the name of the protagonist in "वकील की बेटी" and what is her primary occupation at the start of the story?
questions.a: The protagonist is the unnamed narrator (a woman), and her primary occupation is domestic work in multiple households. A wrong answer (e.g., naming the lawyer's daughter as protagonist) reveals confusion between title character and narrative perspective—the chapter title names a supporting character, not the protagonist.

questions.q: How does the author use the protagonist's internal monologue to establish her dignity despite her socioeconomic status? Give one specific example from the text.
questions.a: The protagonist's internal monologue reveals self-respect through thoughts like refusing to feel ashamed of her work ("eq>s oqQN ysuk&nsuk ugha Fkk") and valuing her children's education over others' opinions. A wrong answer focusing only on external actions misses the author's technique of using first-person narration to contrast inner worth with outer circumstances—the dignity exists *because* we hear her unspoken judgments.

questions.q: Using the PEEL structure, write a paragraph analyzing how the protagonist's interaction with the lawyer's daughter (lquhy) reveals her desire for self-improvement.
questions.a: Point: The protagonist shows quiet ambition through her response to lquhy's encouragement. Evidence: When lquhy offers to teach her, she thinks "eSa lksprh fd lpeqp gh og eq>s cgqr pkgrs gSa" and later accepts writing materials. Explanation: Her internal acceptance contrasts with external hesitation, showing dignity-driven motivation rather than desperate gratitude. Link: This interaction catalyzes her transformation from passive worker to active learner. Wrong answers typically list events without analyzing the psychological subtext revealed through narrative access to her thoughts.

questions.q: Compare the protagonist's relationship with her husband (rkrq'k) and with the lawyer's daughter (lquhy). How do these two relationships differently shape her character development?
questions.a: With rkrq'k: mutual intellectual partnership, shared literary aspirations, emotional anchor ("rkrq'k osQ ;gk¡ tc igq¡prh vkSj og crkrs fd muosQ fdlh caèkq us muls fiQj esjs i<+kbZ&fy[kkbZ osQ ckjs esa iwNk gS rks [kq'kh esa eSa og lc Hkwy tkrh"). With lquhy: catalytic mentorship, initial kindness enabling literacy, but later class distance emerges. The husband relationship sustains long-term growth; the employer relationship initiates it but cannot transcend class barriers. Wrong answers treat both as simply "supportive" without analyzing power dynamics—rkrq'k is a partner; lquhy is a benefactor whose support has limits.

questions.q: Critique the author's choice to keep the protagonist unnamed throughout the story. Does this strengthen or weaken her characterization as a representative of marginalized women?
questions.a: Strengthens: The anonymity universalizes her experience—she represents countless invisible domestic workers. Her identity emerges through actions and voice, not a name. The moment she gains literary recognition ("vk'kkiw.kkZ nsoh"), she's still introduced through her writing, not a personal name. This mirrors how society sees the work before the person. Weakens: Some may argue it denies individual agency. A strong evaluation acknowledges both but concludes the artistic choice serves the thematic purpose of collective representation. Wrong answers pick one side without textual support for the counter-perspective.

questions.q: Write a diary entry from the protagonist's perspective on the day she receives her first payment for writing, capturing her voice, vocabulary level, and emotional complexity.
questions.a: A strong entry uses simple but dignified Hindi, references specific textual details (husband's reaction, children's pride, the physical sensation of holding money earned from words), and shows conflicting emotions: joy at validation, grief for mother who didn't live to see it, fear of whether she can sustain it. Poor entries use sophisticated vocabulary inconsistent with her character or miss the bittersweet layer beneath the triumph—the money matters because it buys her children's future, not because it proves her worth.
